input.quote: In consideration for the licenses granted to Corio pursuant to Section 2 of this Agreement, Corio shall pay the license fees specified in EXHIBIT B hereto. Payment terms of such license fees shall be as set forth in EXHIBIT B hereto.
input.rationale: We reviewed every payment and termination location: Section 4 (Fees), Exhibit B Pricing/Revenue Sharing and Exhibit B Payment Terms (Section 17), Section 11 (Term and Termination), Section 9 (Limitation of Liability) and Sections 13-14. Corio's only monetary obligations are ordinary consideration - license fees, annual maintenance and support fees, MarketSite.net access fees, implementation/professional fees on a time-and-materials basis capped by the Statement of Work, and revenue-share payments - all payable for services actually received. There is no liquidated damages provision, penalty, late-payment or interest charge, minimum-fee-on-termination or early-termination fee payable by Corio anywhere in the Agreement; Section 11 contains no termination charge, and the only post-termination payments are continued fees for the ongoing customer use and support Corio elects to keep receiving (Section 11.3). The audit true-up in Section 4.4 is reciprocal shortfall/overpayment reconciliation, and reimbursement of examination cost on a >5% underpayment is a cost-recovery mechanic tied to actual audit expense, not a stipulated penalty. Termination-related money runs in our favour (refunds of prepaid fees under Sections 3 and 7). The Agreement therefore meets the preferred LD position - Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties - and no redline is warranted.
